item.title: New Source Layer — CRM as Operational Evidence
item.lead: The public documentation of Infloww makes it possible to describe the software layer much more precisely without speculating about hidden databases.

blocks.text: Infloww documents that teams can view fan information such as spending history, purchase frequency, latest and highest expenses, location, local time, manually entered salary information, and notes. The system also includes segmentation based on spending power and purchasing behavior.

The significance of this is methodologically important. It does not prove that every agency collects psychological vulnerabilities. It does prove that a commercial system technically enables the combination of personal context and purchasing behavior with communication and retention. That is a verifiable design fact.

For a true forensic audit, the following artifacts are therefore essential: roles and permissions, audit logs, data fields, exports, retention periods, data processing agreements, sub-processors, data locations, and configurations of automated messages. Screenshots of the interface are useful, but logs are stronger.

blocks.label: EVIDENCE THRESHOLD
blocks.text: The vendor documentation supports the presence of segmentation and personalization features. It does not, by itself, support the claim that specific agencies misuse these features.
Product page Design/function High for feature existence
Help center Detailed operation High for operational design
